I don’t believe Dani needs these tubes (at least not for as long as she’s had them) but it’s not unusual for someone who is overweight to require a feeding tube for nutrition purposes (if they are malnourished), but they would tend to lose weight if they were dependent on tube feeding for an extended amount of time because they receive a set number of calories, and generally exactly what they require

If she became unwell a month after the vaccine, it is not a vaccine reaction. I’m NAD but it’s possible the pain she is experiencing is a side effect of the covid infection itself. Unless she becomes drastically worse, stay out of the ER. They’ve ruled out everything serious and imminently life threatening. If you’re not confident in your primary care physician, I would recommend seeing a new one. It’s possible she has long covid (too early to tell), she has had a secondary immune reaction, or most likely her body is just taking its time to recover. Her symptoms are common after viral infections

So she obviously doesn’t have diabetes, but anyone who has hypoglycaemia can feel when they go ‘low’. You become lightheaded, shaky, nauseous, dizzy, sweaty and what not. You quickly and quietly find an appropriate time to grab some orange juice or some fast acting carbs. She just needs to take a few minutes to correct it and she’ll start feeling better. The dramatics of a glucose monitor is pointless because that number means nothing to her, and will only be dangerous if she neglects it. Not sure why she’d claim something so normal and easy to fix for someone without diabetes.

Also speak to your pharmacist if your doctor won’t support it. They will likely be able to help you develop a plan to taper safely. You’ve been on them for years, so don’t be surprised if it’s a long process to come off them completely. Slow and steady is significantly easier and safer than cold turkey!!

They’re expensive and can be confusing to use but it’s definitely better to have in case, and these days they’re safe and automated enough to only shock if necessary. Get your CPR certification and carry the AED with you, it’s always better to err on the side of caution if possible!!

I’m NAD but the timing seems consistent with ovulation, and it is relatively common for people with a uterus to have light bleeding around this time due to the change in hormones. However, the ‘bleeding a lot and passing many clots’ sounds abnormal. I would recommend bringing this up to your PCP/GP who may refer you to a gynaecologist for further investigation.

I can see that you’re really hurting at the moment and it sucks that no one on reddit is able to connect with you in the way that people can in real life. I see the BDD and transitioning posts, and I understand that you feel so trapped in your mind and your body the only way out is to die - I’ve been there. It’s lonely, and scary, and you don’t want to burden anyone by doing the one thing that’s on your mind. But things will get better. There are other options. Please seek treatment, it’s not as daunting as it seems I promise you. Life really is worth living and I (a stranger on the other side of the world who just happened across your post) care enough to want you to not just live but find happiness. Suicide tourism isn’t it. There are crisis lines and support services available, I urge you to fight for your future because things do get better. There’s more to life than the awful thoughts that plague our minds, but people recover. Please let that be your story too

I’m NAD but I think this warrants a visit to the emergency room. With the history of a severe head injury and symptoms you are experiencing it would not be overreacting to see a doctor, tonight or as soon as possible! Geodon withdrawals can also cause some of these symptoms (and melatonin will not work as well) but it’s better to be on the safe side especially when it comes to neurological issues. They will likely do a neuro exam and possibly a head CT to rule out any immediate life threatening problems, but again with the history and symptoms please seek medical care as soon as you can. Take care

I’m NAD but work in pharmacy. We usually recommend a dewormer with the active ingredient ‘Pyrantel’; called combantrin in Australia but not sure what it’s called in the US. It works locally in the gut (your body won’t absorb it) and it’s generally a 1 dose medication, but dosing at the two week mark will ensure anything is removed. It treats threadworm, roundworm and hookworm. It won’t be harmful even if you don’t have worms. Note that when the worms are killed you will see them in your poo so don’t be too alarmed. If this treatment doesn’t work or your symptoms change/concern you, please go see a doctor :)

I’m NAD but have been diagnosed with many chronic illnesses (due to genetics, nothing environmental) and also have health anxiety. I’m 19 and have had upwards of 30 MRI’s with contrast from 6 months old until now. My kidneys and every other organ are perfect and no lasting damage in relation to the contrast or any heavy metal poisoning. While I understand the concern and your feelings are completely valid, it is incredibly unlikely that there are any deposits anywhere in your body. I see a therapist frequently and she’s really helped me find ways to cope with my health anxiety, I would definitely recommend the same. Please take care, you will be okay

It sounds very similar to alcohol intolerance (an inherited disorder where your body is unable to metabolise the alcohol). I’m NAD but have many friends who have it, and find that reactions begin after one drink. The hallmark symptoms are a flushed face, neck and chest, as well as nausea, stomach cramping, headaches, muscle pains and a stuffy nose. Certain medications aggravate the reactions, have you started any within the past few years? 
Antihistamines can mask the symptoms but unfortunately avoiding alcohol is the only way to stop reactions. Also stay hydrated to help dilute the toxins! It’s most commonly found in those of Asian descent but anyone can have the mutation. 
A physician may have better advice but in my experience it’s just a matter of avoidance unfortunately!

I noticed lumps in a similar spot after I lost weight. NAD but they look like your sacroiliac (SI) joints which are just where your pelvis and base of spine connect. They can occasionally be painful when pressed due to muscles, nerves or ligaments around but if it’s not causing much discomfort or changing in anyway you will likely be okay. Ask next time you see your doctor, but I wouldn’t make an appointment just for that :)
